response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-19
CLINICAL INDICATION: On treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Increasing shortness of breath over one week.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. M. Castellanos (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-09-02
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same projection. The prior is displayed with higher contrast than the current, which is softer and flatter. The prior appears mildly rotated and the current appears straight. Both differences limit comparison of subtle density change, hilar size and mediastinal contour.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None time-sensitive. No finding is flagged time-sensitive. Triage urgency is high and an on-call page is not indicated. The first item for review is the left hilum, where change is unresolved between the two blind reads.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is central with the expected slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch. No central airway narrowing at this resolution. Lung volumes are large. No focal consolidation, collapse or discrete mass in any zone. Mildly coarse markings in the right lower zone, with mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base and no focal consolidation. Overlying soft tissue may contribute to the right lower zone haze. Pattern and extent are similar on the prior. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. A tiny density over the right medial upper zone is seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, and similar to the prior. Upper mediastinum is not widened. Right hilum is unremarkable. Left hilum is not bulky on the current study and shows a small ring lucency, possibly a bronchus seen end-on. The left hilum looks fuller and denser on the prior. Left hilar change is INDETERMINATE: one read called it indeterminate and smaller, the other called it stable and similar, so the reads did not agree. Differences in contrast and rotation may explain the appearance.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles are sharp on both studies. No pleural line and no visible pleural thickening. Diaphragm: left dome is level with or slightly higher than the right on both studies, with gas-filled bowel and stomach beneath it and no gas under the right dome. Gas distension under the left dome is INDETERMINATE: the two reads disagreed (one stable, one decreased). The prior appears more distended.
- Heart: Heart is not enlarged on this PA film, at the upper limit of normal, with sharp borders. Size and contour are similar to the prior.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion at this resolution. Degenerative change at both shoulders and in the lower cervical spine. No soft tissue gas. Fine bone detail is limited. Device: left-sided central venous catheter crossing the midline, tip projecting over the expected level of the superior vena cava, same course and tip position as the prior. No new device.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Left hilum appears less full and denser-looking on the current than the prior (described in words only, no measurements). This is indeterminate because of the contrast and rotation differences, and the reads did not agree. Gas distension under the left dome appears less on the current, indeterminate, reads disagreed. Tiny right medial upper zone density seen on the prior only, not clearly seen on the current.
- Unchanged: Coarse right lower zone markings, aortic knuckle and mediastinal width, heart size and contour, sharp costophrenic angles, dome relationship, and left central venous catheter position. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the left hilum truly smaller on the current study than on the prior? | Reason: The prior has higher contrast and mild rotation, and both can make one hilum look larger and denser. A frontal film alone does not separate vessel from node or mass. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast, and review of the source images in PACS.
- Is the tiny density over the right medial upper zone on the prior a lung nodule or first rib costochondral calcification? | Reason: The density is well under the size at which X-ray separates a nodule from bone or a vessel end-on. It is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. CT chest if it persists on review.
- Is there opacity behind the heart or at the left base? | Reason: The relatively high left dome and gas-filled bowel overlap the left base and retrocardiac region on a frontal film alone. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.
- Is there a focal bone lesion in the ribs, shoulders or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS.
- Is the left hilar fullness vascular (pulmonary artery) or nodal? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessel from lymph node, and the difference in image contrast between the two studies limits judgment of subtle density change. | Recommend: Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging. If none is available, contrast-enhanced CT chest.
- Is the small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study a bronchus seen end-on or a small cavitary or cystic focus? | Reason: The structure is small, overlaps hilar vessels, and is seen on a downsampled frontal image only. It is less conspicuous on the higher-contrast prior. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. Lateral view or CT chest if it persists.
- Does the asymmetry of the breast shadows reflect previous left breast surgery, or positioning? | Reason: Soft-tissue contours are partly outside the field and faint at this resolution. The asymmetry makes the right lower zone look hazier than the left on both studies. | Recommend: Correlate with surgical history. Do not read the right lower zone haze as lung opacity without that correlation.
- What is the exact catheter tip position relative to the cavoatrial junction, and what type of line is it? | Reason: The carina and the right atrial junction are not sharply defined on these images, and the insertion site and any reservoir lie outside the field. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Correlate with the line insertion record.
- Are there small nodules in the retrocardiac region, at the apices or behind the diaphragm domes? | Reason: Only a single frontal view of each study is available. These areas are hidden by overlap, and small nodules cannot be separated from vessels seen end-on or from rib ends. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, and fine bone detail such as cortex, pedicles and small lucent lesions is not reliably shown. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.

IMPRESSION:
1. Left hilum: change since the prior is indeterminate. The current appears less full than the prior, but contrast and rotation differences limit the comparison and the two reads did not agree. Vessel versus node cannot be separated on this frontal film.
2. Small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study, possibly a bronchus seen end-on. A cavitary or cystic focus is not excluded (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
3. Coarse right lower zone markings, unchanged from the prior, without focal consolidation. Overlying soft tissue may contribute.
4. Mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base, similar to the prior, without focal consolidation.
5. Heart not enlarged, at the upper limit of normal, similar to the prior.
6. Gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate. The reads disagreed on whether it is stable or decreased.
7. In the setting of breathlessness, no new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new nodule or mass is seen compared with the prior on this single frontal film, and heart size is similar. The film does not show a cause for the breathlessness. Left central venous catheter and aortic knuckle are unchanged.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the left hilar question (interval not specified in the findings, for resident and attending to set).
- Lateral view or CT chest for the retrocardiac and left base question and for possible small nodules.
- Review the source images in PACS for the left hilar ring lucency, the right upper zone density, the catheter tip and bone detail.
- Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging, the line insertion record and the surgical history.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
